tool.name: write_deliverable
tool.description: Write a structured deliverable artifact under the shared deliverables root so downstream agents can consume it without inheriting your message history.
tool.details:
Use this instead of writing handoff files with `str_replace_editor`.
Root path: /workspace/.strix/deliverables/
The `path` parameter is RELATIVE to that root. Conventional layout: - recon/attack_surface.md (black-box recon output) - pre-recon/code_map.md (white-box code understanding output) - findings/<class>/<id>.md (one file per suspected finding) - pocs/<finding-id>.md (one file per confirmed PoC) - reports/<id>.md (optional: draft report content)
The file is created (with parent dirs) or OVERWRITTEN on each call. To append, first read_deliverable then write the concatenated content.

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: Relative path under /workspace/.strix/deliverables/. No leading '/' or '..' segments. Example: "findings/xss/001.md".

parameter.name: content
parameter.description: Full textual content of the deliverable. Markdown recommended for readability; JSON fine for structured queues.

returns.description: Response containing: - success: Whether the write succeeded - path: Absolute path of the written file - bytes_written: Size of the written content

tool.examples:
# A recon agent writes an attack-surface map
recon/attack_surface.md # Attack surface for example.com
## Subdomains - www.example.com - api.example.com (REST) - admin.example.com (403 without auth, bypass suspected)
## Endpoints worth testing - POST /api/v1/login (user-controlled JSON body) - GET /search?q= (reflects query unsanitized)
# A discovery agent writes a single finding
findings/xss/001.md # XSS-001: Reflected XSS in /search
- Source: query param `q` on GET /search - Sink: HTML body, no encoding observed - Context: HTML_BODY - Witness payload: <script>1</script> - Confidence: high - Notes: No CSP; likely cookie exfil impact.

tool.name: read_deliverable
tool.description: Read a deliverable artifact written by you or another agent.
tool.details: Path is relative to /workspace/.strix/deliverables/, matching the convention from write_deliverable. Returns the full file content. If you just want to discover what's available, call list_deliverables first.

returns.description: Response containing: - success: Whether the read succeeded - path: Absolute path of the file - content: Full text content of the deliverable

tool.examples:
# An exploit agent pulls the finding it was told to validate
findings/xss/001.md

tool.name: list_deliverables
tool.description: List deliverables written by agents in this run, optionally filtered by a kind prefix. Use this at the start of your work to discover what upstream agents have produced.
tool.details: Returns path, size, and a short preview (first content line) for each deliverable. Pass `kind` to scope to a subdirectory like "findings", "findings/xss", "recon", "pocs".

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: Optional path prefix under the deliverables root (e.g. "findings/xss"). Omit to list everything.

returns.description: Response containing: - success: Whether the list succeeded - deliverables: List of matching deliverables with path/size/preview - total_count: Number of deliverables returned - root: The deliverables root directory

tool.examples:
# An exploit-phase agent discovers what the discovery phase wrote
findings/xss
# A reporting agent scans the whole set
